desc: The Senado Federal is the upper chamber of Brazil's National Congress, composed of 81 senators - three for each of the 26 states and the Federal District - elected to eight-year terms, with the constitutional powers of legislative revision, treaty approval, confirmation of senior appointments and the summoning of ministers and officials to give evidence. Its relevance to this board is carried by Senator Eduardo Girão of Ceará (Senate member code 5976, elected for the 56th legislature and continuing into the 57th), who has pressed publicly for the Brazilian state's UAP record to be opened and who brought the January 1996 Varginha case to Capitol Hill on its thirtieth anniversary in 2026. Brazil is a comparative test case for the concealment thesis in a way few countries are: its military UFO files were transferred to the Arquivo Nacional and made citizen-accessible, and the 1986 air force incident is documented in that archive, so Brazil has already done what the American programme is alleged to be preventing. A national legislature that can summon officials, and that contains a member actively pursuing the Varginha file, is a live route by which the non-US half of the record can be forced open - and it is a route the United States cannot classify. No primary Senate legislative instrument on UAP was located in this pass; the Senate's keyword search service for legislative matters has been deprecated and its replacement returns unfiltered results.

claims.text: Requerimento no 193, de 2022 (RQS 193/2022) was authored by Senador Eduardo Girao (PODEMOS/CE) with co-signatories Paulo Rocha (PT/PA), Izalci Lucas (PSDB/DF), Reguffe (PODEMOS/DF), Jorge Kajuru (PODEMOS/GO), Marcos do Val (PODEMOS/ES), Alessandro Vieira (CIDADANIA/SE) and Eliziane Gama (CIDADANIA/MA), and was presented and read on 16 March 2022.

The ementa of RQS 193/2022 is 'Sessao especial destinada a comemorar os 75 anos do Dia Mundial da Ufologia'. Its nature is recorded as 'Realizacao de sessao especial ou comemoracao no periodo do expediente'. It is a request for a commemorative plenary session under Article 199 of the Regimento Interno do Senado Federal, not an instrument compelling the production of records.

The requerimento was approved by the Plenary on 16 March 2022 and the special session was held on 24 June 2022; its tramitacao is closed, with the last recorded location the Coordenacao de Arquivo on 29 June 2022.

claims.text: The instrument's official publications are: Diario do Senado Federal no 32 of 17 March 2022, pages 269 to 275 and page 62; and Diario do Senado Federal no 99 of 25 June 2022, pages 7 to 67 recording the special session.

The justificacao of RQS 193/2022 names Operacao Prato (1977), the creation of SIOANI in 1969 at the IV Comando Aereo Regional in Sao Paulo, and the 1986 'Noite Oficial dos UFOs no Brasil' as official Brazilian government UFO research programmes run through the Aeronautica.

The justificacao states that a search of the Arquivo Nacional for the term OVNI alone returns 137 registros, while a search on the specific reference code BR DFANBSB ARX returns 758 documents, some over 70 years old.

The justificacao states that from 2007 the Aeronautica, but not the Exercito and not the Marinha, began sending its research papers to the Arquivo Nacional in Brasilia, totalling more than 20,000 pages of released files.

The justificacao records that in August 2010 the then commander of the FAB determined, by an instrument published in the Diario Oficial da Uniao, that all OVNI cases registered across the force's installations be concentrated at COMDABRA for transmission to the Arquivo Nacional.

The justificacao asserts that Brazil was the first nation to officially admit that OVNIs exist and are of extraterrestrial provenance, at a 1954 session at the Escola Superior de Guerra in Rio de Janeiro addressed by the then Aeronautica captain Joao Adil de Oliveira, with France following in 1976.
The justificacao states that the Aeronautica was always discreet about these matters but never denied them when questioned.

The justificacao cites the 2021 Pentagon UAP report as examining 144 sighting cases of which only one was explained, and cites the omnibus funding bill signed by President Biden on 15 March 2022 including 782.5 billion dollars for defence with resources reserved for UAP research legislated within the FY2022 National Defense Authorization Act.

The Senate file for the matter lodges individual presentation documents dated 24 June 2022 for invited speakers Rony Vernet, Ademar Jose, Gary Heseltine, Geraldo Lemos Neto, Inajar Antonio Kurowski, Jackson Luiz Camargo, Robert Lambert Salas and Thiago Ticchetti.

dossier.denialPosture: None on the part of the Senate. The chamber's posture is the inverse of denial: it approved a plenary session on the subject unanimously enough to be recorded simply as 'Aprovada pelo Plenario', gave the floor to foreign and domestic witnesses including a former US Air Force officer, and entered into its permanent Diario the specific archive reference code under which its own military's files can be retrieved.
dossier.narrative:
The premise that most needs correcting before this node is usable is the shape of the instrument. RQS 193/2022 is a requerimento, a procedural request, filed under Article 199 of the Regimento Interno do Senado Federal, asking for a special session at an appropriate date to commemorate 75 years of World Ufology Day. It carries the signatures of Eduardo Girao (PODEMOS/CE), Eliziane Gama (CIDADANIA/MA), Alessandro Vieira (CIDADANIA/SE), Izalci Lucas (PSDB/DF), Jorge Kajuru (PODEMOS/GO), Marcos do Val (PODEMOS/ES), Paulo Rocha (PT/PA) and Reguffe (PODEMOS/DF), which is a cross-party spread from left to right. It was read and approved on 16 March 2022, published in the Diario do Senado Federal no 32 of 17 March 2022 at pages 269 to 275 and page 62, the session was held on 24 June 2022 and published in DSF no 99 of 25 June 2022 at pages 7 to 67, and the matter was closed and sent to the archive coordination on 29 June 2022. It compelled nothing and produced no documents. Any claim on this board that the Senate passed an instrument seeking UAP records must be retired.

What survives, and what makes the node worth keeping, is the justificacao. Brazilian requerimentos carry a reasoning section that enters the permanent record with the instrument, and Girao's runs to several pages of institutional history. It states that Brazil was the first nation to officially admit that OVNIs exist and have extraterrestrial provenance, at a 1954 session at the Escola Superior de Guerra in Rio at which the then Aeronautica captain Joao Adil de Oliveira spoke to officers, civilians and press, and that France followed only in 1976. It states that since 1954 the Brazilian government has created several official UFO research programmes through the Aeronautica, naming Operacao Prato in 1977, SIOANI in 1969 at the IV Comando Aereo Regional in Sao Paulo, and the 1986 night in which 21 spherical objects, each given as 100 metres in diameter, were pursued for hours by Brazilian jet fighters. It states that the Aeronautica was always discreet about these facts but never denied them when asked. It states that from 2007 the Aeronautica, and expressly not the Exercito and not the Marinha, began sending its papers to the Arquivo Nacional, and that the total now exceeds 20,000 pages. It records that in August 2010 the then FAB commander determined by an instrument published in the Diario Oficial da Uniao that all OVNI cases across the force be concentrated at COMDABRA for onward transmission. It records the April 2013 meeting at the Ministry of Defence, convened at the invitation of then Foreign Minister Celso Amorim and held before the service commanders, at which researchers pressed for the Army and Navy files. And it gives the archive arithmetic directly: searching OVNI alone yields 137 registros, but the reference code BR DFANBSB ARX yields 758 documents, some of them more than 70 years old.

The justificacao also turns outward, and that is where the comparison it enables becomes explicit. It notes that at least 30 nations established research commissions, that the 2021 Pentagon UAP preliminary assessment examined 144 sighting cases of which only one was explained, and that on 15 March 2022 President Biden signed an omnibus funding bill including 782.5 billion dollars for defence with resources reserved for unexplained aerial phenomena research legislated within the FY2022 National Defense Authorization Act. Brazil, in other words, put the American record into its own legislative record while noting that its own files were already open.

The session itself, on 24 June 2022, was held in the Senate plenary and is documented in the Senate's own file with individual presentation documents lodged for each invited speaker: Rony Vernet, Ademar Jose, Gary Heseltine, Geraldo Lemos Neto, Inajar Antonio Kurowski, Jackson Luiz Camargo, Robert Lambert Salas and Thiago Ticchetti. Agencia Senado's report of the session records Gevaerd calling the opening incomplete but fruitful, Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, describing unidentified objects disabling ten nuclear weapons at a launch facility he commanded, and the delivery to Girao at the close of a document the participants called the Carta de Brasilia, recommending creation of a permanent joint civil and military commission to enable organised research on the subject.

One error must be named and buried. A previous pass on this board asserted that Senator Girao brought the 1996 Varginha case to Capitol Hill in 2026. Nothing in the reporting located supports that. Girao's verified, documented action is RQS 193/2022 and the 24 June 2022 special session, and the board should carry that and nothing beyond it.
openQuestions: A previous research pass asserted that Senator Girao brought the 1996 Varginha case to Capitol Hill in 2026. No source located supports this. It should be treated as retracted unless a primary record is produced.

No Brazilian legislative instrument has been located that compels production of Army or Navy holdings, establishes a records review board, or creates the permanent joint commission proposed in the Carta de Brasilia.
The text of the Carta de Brasilia itself has not been retrieved; its content is known only through Agencia Senado's summary.
Whether any of the eight co-signatory senators pursued follow-on action after the session closed on 29 June 2022 is not established.

The full stenographic record of the 24 June 2022 session is published in DSF no 99, pages 7 to 67, but has not been read in this pass; individual statements beyond those summarised by Agencia Senado are unverified.

Several factual assertions inside the justificacao, notably the 100-metre diameter figure for the 1986 objects and the primacy claim for Brazil in 1954, are the author's assertions entered into the record, not independently verified findings.
dossier.whatItIs: The Senado Federal is the upper chamber of Brazil's National Congress. On 16 March 2022 it received Requerimento no 193, de 2022 (RQS 193/2022), tabled by Senator Eduardo Girao (PODEMOS/CE) with seven co-signatories, and approved it the same day; the resulting special plenary session was held on 24 June 2022. The requerimento's stated purpose was to hold a special session commemorating the 75th anniversary of World Ufology Day, and its justificacao entered into the Senate's permanent record a detailed account of Brazil's official UFO programmes and archive holdings.
dossier.whyImplicated: The Senate node is where the correction lives, and correcting it makes the comparison stronger rather than weaker. RQS 193/2022 is not a records-production instrument. Its ementa is a request for a commemorative special session under Article 199 of the Senate's internal rules, and its disposition reads 'Aprovada pelo Plenario' followed by 'SESSAO REALIZADA'. What it did instead is arguably more useful to this board: it wrote into the permanent legislative record of a G20 state, over eight senators' names, that the Aeronautica ran Operacao Prato and SIOANI, that FAB fighters chased 21 objects in 1986, that from 2007 the air force but not the army and not the navy transferred its files, and that the archive reference code BR DFANBSB ARX returns 758 documents. No US congressional instrument has ever put an equivalent set of specifics into the record as settled institutional history. The contrast is not that Brazil compelled disclosure through legislation. It is that Brazil did not have to, because the executive had already published, and the legislature's role was to hold a session about it in the plenary chamber with foreign witnesses at the rostrum.
